title: Search a 2D Matrix II
statement: You are given an `m x n` grid of integers `matrix`. Reading any row from left to right, the values never go down, and reading any column from top to bottom, the values never go down either. Return `true` when `target` is one of the values in `matrix`, and `false` when it is not. Try to do better than checking every cell.
constraints: Every row is sorted in ascending order
Every column is sorted in ascending order
notes:
## Intuition

Scanning every cell answers the question in O(m·n) but ignores the ordering. Look at the top-right corner instead: everything to its left is smaller or equal, and everything below it is bigger or equal. So one comparison there throws away a whole column (when the corner is too big) or a whole row (when it is too small). Walking from that corner like a staircase, the two edges of the remaining rectangle only ever move inwards, just like two pointers closing in from opposite ends.

## Approach

1. Start with `row` at the top row and `col` at the last column.
2. While both are inside the grid, read `value = matrix[row][col]`.
3. If `value` equals `target`, return `true`.
4. If `value` is bigger, every cell below it in this column is at least as big, so move `col` one step left.
5. Otherwise every cell to its left in this row is at most `value`, too small, so move `row` one step down.
6. If the walk leaves the grid, `target` is not there: return `false`.

## Example 1, step by step

`target = 5`. Start at `row = 0, col = 4`: `15 > 5`, so `col = 3`; `11 > 5`, so `col = 2`; `7 > 5`, so `col = 1`; `4 < 5`, so `row = 1`; now `matrix[1][1] = 5` equals the target and the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m + n): each step removes one row or one column, and there are only m + n of them.
- Space: O(1): just two indices.

## Pitfalls

- Starting at the top-left (or bottom-right) corner does not work: both neighbours move the value the same way, so a comparison cannot rule anything out.
- Check both bounds in the loop condition: `row` can run off the bottom and `col` off the left.
- Rows are sorted but a row does not start after the previous row ends (unlike Search a 2D Matrix), so you cannot flatten the grid into one sorted list.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `row` | current row; every row above it has been ruled out |
| `col` | current column; every column to its right has been ruled out |
| `value` | the number at the current corner of the remaining rectangle |

narration.3: ...at the last column: the top-right corner, where left means smaller and down means bigger.
narration.5: Keep walking while the position is still inside the grid.
narration.6: Read the number at the current corner of the unexplored rectangle.
narration.7: Is it the number we want?
narration.10: Too big: everything further down this column is at least as big.
narration.11: So drop this column and step left.
narration.13: Too small: everything further left in this row is at most this big, so drop the row and step down.
narration.16: The walk left the grid without a match, so the target is absent.
